Edge AI is a hardware contract — wearing a model costume
blocks.sub: Deadline engineering, scene-aware drift and hardware interlocks

blocks.x: Computer Vision & Edge AI is delivered by an Achala practice team that stays through industrialization. Achala connects devices, twins and control loops with rollback built in: firmware staged and signed, actuation authorized and logged, model drift measured against reality. Physical operations get software-grade discipline. Who this is for: plant, fleet and device operations leaders, and engineering heads accountable for safe actuation.

The discipline mirrors the vision domain's standards but adds the edge: quantization-aware evaluation, thermal and power budgets as release gates, and fleet heterogeneity treated as a release-train problem.

widgets.title: Frame to decision — click stages for the fleet contract

stages.name: Capture
stages.detail: Per-camera health telemetry (fps, focus, illumination) with auto-flagging; a drifting camera quarantines its frames rather than poisoning the eval.

stages.name: Preprocess
stages.detail: Resolution normalization and per-hour lighting profiles — transforms recorded for training so inference never drifts from training assumptions.

stages.name: Infer
stages.detail: INT8 models per hardware class with measured accuracy deltas; uncertain frames (low confidence, disagreement) escalate with crops attached.

stages.name: Decide
stages.detail: Task-level decisions (defect class, presence, count) with grounding evidence — bounding boxes and crops stored for the audit trail.

stages.name: Learn
stages.detail: Uncertain frames route to labeling with provenance; the retraining loop runs monthly with fleet-drift fixes staged per hardware class.

widgets.note: The learn stage is what keeps the fleet honest — production frames are the training set, and drift feeds the next version rather than the incident report.

The deadline is the contract
blocks.sub: Hardware-fit models, deadline checks and scene-aware drift, edge AI as an engineering discipline

blocks.x: Edge vision fails when models are trained in the lab and deployed to hardware they do not fit: the quantized model misses its frame budget, the accelerator thermal-throttles at noon, and the line keeps moving while the QA gate goes blind. The discipline starts from the hardware contract, models quantized and shaped to the accelerator's budget, deadline checks enforced per frame (a late inference is a dropped inference, logged), and thermal/power envelopes tested under production conditions. The safety interlock path stays hardware-wired: vision may advise; it may never be the last line between a person and a hazard.

Drift at the edge is scene drift, lighting changes with seasons, product SKUs change with campaigns, camera lenses get dirty, so monitors watch scene statistics alongside model scores, and release trains stage canary devices before line-wide rollout. The console reads deadline adherence, drift alarms and per-device model currency; the retraining loop is fed from the hard negatives the deadline check and drift monitors surface.

items: Quantized to the accelerator's real budget, tested under thermal load.
Late inferences are dropped and logged, the blind gate is visible.
Lighting, SKU and lens drift monitored alongside model scores.
Vision advises; hardware stops. The last line is not a model.
Why is edge AI a "hardware contract"?

Because the deadline is physical: a model that misses 84ms on the line SKU is worthless regardless of accuracy. Each SKU class signs accuracy, p99 latency and power together, the triple is the contract, and the gates enforce all three.
How do you handle model drift on the line?

The drift overlay: canary frames re-scored against the golden set, drift alarms with signed tolerances, and a retraining loop that re-earns the deadline on the target hardware before a model ships to the fleet.
Can you work with our existing cameras and PLCs?

Yes, the integration surface names cameras, PLCs and quality systems. Capture contracts pin resolution, timing and lighting conditions, because the frame the model sees must be the frame the contract tested.
What happens when lighting or conditions change on the floor?

Condition changes are part of the eval set: the golden set includes your worst shifts, and the gates require deadline-holding accuracy across them, a model that only works in lab lighting never reaches the line.
What do operations and quality inherit?
The console with deadline adherence as the headline, the drift drills, the eval sets and the retrain calendar, quality sees accuracy evidence per shift, operations sees the hardware contract holding.
